habitat: Usually singly on coastal or inland waters. It is shy. When flushed it towers up and flies some distance.
summary: A common summer visitor, with a few present all year. A large, long-legged wader with clear white underparts, a slightly upturned black bill, and green-grey legs that the identification line calls greenish. The back and rump are extensively white in flight. On take-off it calls a loud triple tew-tew-tew. Newman does not name the months. The Kemp name Greenshank and the code NB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Marsh Sandpiper is smaller, with a straight slender bill and yellowish legs. Greenshank has a more robust, slightly upturned bill and green-grey legs.

bill.shape: Slightly upturned and more robust than Marsh Sandpiper.

head.pattern: Legs are greenish on the identification line and green-grey in the description, so no single leg colour is stored.

upperparts.pattern: Sandy-brown above, with white feather edges. The back is white in the identification line, and the flight description says an extensive white back and rump.

wings.pattern: The feet protrude slightly in flight.

Clear white underparts. The legs are greenish, also described as green-grey.
The identification line includes a white back.
Extensive white back and rump. The feet protrude slightly.
White underparts. The underwing colour is not given.

calls.description: On take-off it calls a loud triple 'tew-tew-tew'. No grade A recording from South Africa was found. The selected file is a grade A call from Sweden. The filename is Gluttsnappalocklate.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common summer visitor, with a few present all year, and does not name the months, so status is summer-migrant and monthsPresent is unset. The legs are greenish and green-grey, so no single colour is stored. Sandy-brown is not a vocabulary colour. No grade A recording from South Africa was found; a grade B recording from South Africa exists. The Kemp name Greenshank and the code NB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^9=512 mature individuals (non-breeding visitor); paper interval half–double → 256–1024.
